newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares ease in profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares ease in profit-taking.

text.p: Istanbul shares dropped an average 0.72 percent in profit-taking on Thursday, following a 3.7 percent jump in the last three days, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 ended at 71,533.46, down 517.78 points from Wednesday's two-month high close. It sank to a low of 71,186 in late trade.
Daily volume stood at 18.95 trillion lira, including a 5.82 trillion lira block deal on the wholesale market, after Wednesday's 13.6 trillion.
"There is a strong resistance at the index's 72,000 level. The recent rise was very fast and the market needed to digest it," said Tuncay Cevher from Bank Kapital.

The index had closed just above the 72,000 barrier on Wednesday in a medium-term uptrend fuelled by fresh cash influx and optimism last week when the index soared 7.3 percent. It had passed the critical 70,000 resistance on Tuesday.
"There may be some more profit-taking. The market must get used to carrying costs at 70,000 levels for this uptrend to continue," Cevher said.

Brokers said activity in shares of largely state-owned firms which led the recent rally faded and players switched to utilities and other private sector stocks with bright nine-month profit prospects.

The 85-share industrial index lost 0.7 percent to 78,597.76 and the 15-share financial index eased 0.78 percent to 63,111.08. Of the 224 issues traded, falls outdid rises by 102 to 72 and 50 closed stable.

Top actives were utilities Aktas Elektrik, steady at 54,000 lira, Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,000 lira at 72,000 and Kepez Elektrik, up 1,000 lira at 75,000. Largely state owned flat steel giant Eregli, down 500 lira at 10,000 was also active.
